anchors.favour_price_upper_bound: GDD appendix A.2, as quoted in work order 008: a Stoker offers +600 Crowns for 20 Brass Ingots, 30 Crowns per ingot. A favour price, used as an upper bound.
anchors.market_rate: Proposal: the market sits at half the favour price upper bound, 15 Crowns per Brass Ingot. A Brass Ingot is 108 labour-seconds (prospect copper 54 s + smelt 54 s), so 15/108 Crowns per labour-second, 500 Crowns per hour of labour.
anchors.end_product_price: collector_price = labour-seconds of the whole chain x 15/108, rounded half up, using the placeholder recipe quantities of 1 from work order 004. Brass Key 216 s = 30; Iron Lock 378 s = 52.5, 53; Steel Blade 756 s = 105; Garnet Sight 972 s = 135.
anchors.end_product_cap: Proposal: a collector buys one hour of the product's own final action per week, 3600 / seconds rounded down. Brass Key 108 s = 33; Iron Lock 162 s = 22; Steel Blade 216 s = 16; Garnet Sight 216 s = 16.
anchors.rat_scrap: Proposal: 2 Crowns a unit, capped at one hour of Rust Rat Runt kills a week (3600 / 54 = 66).
anchors.collector_weekly_total: 66 x 2 + 33 x 30 + 22 x 53 + 16 x 105 + 16 x 135 = 6128 Crowns per player per week from rat scrap and the four Rustmoor end products, plus 2009 from Scavenging salvage (see scavenging_salvage) = 8137, plus 840 from the four Act I Curios (see curios) = 8977 Crowns per player per week at most.
anchors.bound: Ledger Pages are bound (GDD section 5). The Foundry Pass is bound and untradable, with no collector and no grocer price, as settled by Jeremy on 22 October 2026 (work order 018, 'Settled after the first draft': 'The Foundry Pass is an item, item.rustmoor.foundry_pass, bound and untradable, with no collector.'); it is the pass that lets a Tinker enter the Cinderworks (GDD section 4, Act I: 'Entering the Cinderworks needs a Foundry Pass'). Scrapjaw's Cleaver is tradable, unbound with no collector, as settled by Jeremy on 22 October 2026 (work order 008). Every other Rustmoor item is unbound; only those listed with a price have a collector.
anchors.cooking_ingredients: Settled (work order 012, 'Settled after review', 22 October 2026: 'Ingredients come from a grocer's counter at the Counting-House window, never locked.'). Barley Meal and Salt Pork are sold only at the grocer's counter at the Counting-House window (GDD section 6: 'The same window has a grocer's counter that sells Cooking ingredients at fixed prices, also never locked.' The Crown budget lists it among the sinks: 'Cooking ingredients from the grocer's counter'). No Rustmoor gathering skill makes food (GDD section 6 Skills table). Prices, settled: Barley Meal 2 Crowns, Salt Pork 4 (work order 012, 'Settled after review', 22 October 2026: 'Ingredients cost about a quarter of the derived price: Barley Meal 2 Crowns, Salt Pork 4.'), held in each item's grocer_price above (tuning.economy/2, work order 013). How the quarter was taken: each ingredient stands in for one gathering action, a level-1 action (54 s) for Barley Meal and a level-5 action (108 s) for Salt Pork; at the market_rate anchor of 15/108 Crowns per labour-second that labour is worth 7.5 and 15 Crowns, which are labour values, not prices, and no one sells or buys either ingredient at them. A quarter is 1.875 and 3.75, set at 2 and 4.
anchors.npc_sell_prices: The grocer's prices are the grocer_price field on each item above (tuning.economy/2, work order 013): item.rustmoor.barley_meal 2, item.rustmoor.salt_pork 4. Settled (work order 012, 'Settled after review', 22 October 2026); sold at the grocer's counter at the Counting-House window, never locked (GDD section 6: 'The same window has a grocer's counter that sells Cooking ingredients at fixed prices, also never locked.'); see cooking_ingredients. The drops check reads the field, not this note.
anchors.cooking_recipes: Accepted (work order 012, 'Settled after review', 22 October 2026: 'Surplus Rations go to the Exchange, and higher Cooking tiers pay only in XP per hour. Both accepted.'): each Cooking action's ingredients stand in for gathering labour equal to its own tier time, and it makes one Ration per 54 s. Level 1: 1 Barley Meal (54 s) makes 1. Level 5: 1 Salt Pork (108 s) makes 2. Level 10: 1 Barley Meal + 1 Salt Pork (162 s) makes 3. Level 15: 2 Barley Meal + 1 Salt Pork (216 s) makes 4. So every tier makes 66.7 Rations per Cooking hour and costs 2 Crowns of grocer ingredients per Ration at every tier (level 1: 2/1; level 5: 4/2; level 10: (2+4)/3; level 15: (2x2+4)/4); higher tiers are worth doing for their higher XP per hour, as in every other skill.
anchors.ration_sink: Derived from settled prices (work order 012, 'Settled after review': 'Levelling Cooking through Rustmoor then removes about 15,000 Crowns, and eating about 4,000'). Every Cooking tier costs 2 Crowns of grocer ingredients per Ration (cooking_recipes), so each figure is Rations x 2. Kill faucet: the drops check's Crown faucet report at 12 combat hours a day, the best non-boss monster at each level: 39200, 40600, 42000, 44100 Crowns a week at the Runt, Scrounger, Tinplate and Gaffer. Band time per tier from the curve (cost_to_next(L) / best XP per hour, divided by 8.4 band-skill hours a day): 0.35, 3.77, 4.62, 5.22 days, 13.96 in all; band kill faucet = sum of tier days x weekly faucet / 7 = 1987 + 21866 + 27698 + 32895 = 84445 Crowns, 42336 a week. (1) Levelling Cooking 1 to 20 at the pacing rate: 117.28 Cooking hours (13.96 days x 8.4), 66.67 Rations an hour at every tier (one per 54 s), so 7819 Rations and 15638 Crowns over the band; a week, 15638 / 13.96 x 7 = 7840 Crowns (3920 Rations). Share of the kill faucet: 15638 / 84445 = 18.5%. (2) Eating at the reference use (content/tuning/combat.json rations.reference_use, revision 7, RATION_HEAL_HP 600, 12 combat hours a day; the figures the drops check's grocer sink report prints): 2085 Rations over the band, 4170 Crowns; a week 2091 Crowns. Share of the kill faucet: 4170 / 84445 = 4.9%. By tier a week: 2329, 1284, 1011, 817 Rations; 4658, 2567, 2022, 1633 Crowns; 11.9%, 6.3%, 4.8%, 3.7% of that tier's faucet. (Before combat.json revision 7 corrected rations.needs.consumption these read 2110 Rations and 4220 Crowns.) The drops check reports both figures against kills plus the collectors' weekly maximum (50473 a week since work order 017, 48464 before), giving 15.5% and 4.1% (16.2% and 4.3% before); the shares here are against kills alone. The two do not add: a player who levels Cooking makes 7819 Rations and eats 2085 of them, so the grocer removes about 15600 Crowns over the band (18.5%) and the surplus goes to the Exchange; a player who only cooks what they eat removes about 4200 (4.9%). Either way the grocer stays well below Calibrating as the main sink (GDD section 6: 'Calibrating is the main Crown sink').
anchors.ration_collector: Proposal (work order 012): no collector buys Rations, Barley Meal or Salt Pork, so Cooking adds no Crown faucet and NPC ingredients cannot be resold to an NPC at a profit. All three are unbound and tradable on the Exchange.
anchors.starter_crate: Settled (work order 012, 'Settled after review', 22 October 2026: 'The starter crate holds 342 Rations, bound to the player, enough for the first 12-hour queue.'). GDD section 7: Brassbuckle 'leaves her 50 Brass Ingots and a crate of Rations from the workshop's old stock'. Derived: the first queue is at most 12 hours (content/tuning/xp-curve.json OFFLINE_HOURS_PER_CHECKIN 12); a new player fights the Rust Rat Runt, 54 s a kill, 66.67 kills an hour, at 0.428 Rations a kill (content/tuning/combat.json rations.reference_use before revision 7), 28.5 Rations an hour; 28.5 x 12 = 342. Combat.json revision 7 corrects the Ration use to 27.72 an hour against the Runt, so the first 12-hour queue eats about 333 and the settled 342 last about 12.3 hours; the count stays 342 as settled. The 342 are bound to the player, while item.rustmoor.rustmoor_ration above is unbound; the bound stack is held in content/start.json (start/1, work order 013) with bound: true. The crate is a grant, not a grocer purchase, so it removes no Crowns.
anchors.scavenging_salvage: Settled (work order 017, 'Settled after the first draft', 22 October 2026: 'The pricing is accepted.'). Scavenging produces 'Wreck salvage' and 'picks over the loose surface' of the tip (GDD section 6, Skills); ore, coal and gems are Prospecting's, so no Scavenging action makes an existing material. Nothing consumes the four salvage items, so each is an end product with a capped collector (work order 004, carried forward: 'Every end product needs a use or a capped buyer'; GDD section 6, The Crown budget, lists 'NPC collectors buying Curios, scrap and crafted goods, capped weekly' as a faucet). Price and cap follow end_product_price and end_product_cap: labour-seconds are the action's own time. Bent Nails 54 s x 15/108 = 7.5, 8, cap 3600/54 = 66; Umbrella Ribs 108 s = 15, cap 33; Odd Spoons 162 s = 22.5, 23, cap 22; Clock Movement 216 s = 30, cap 16. Weekly maximum: 66 x 8 + 33 x 15 + 22 x 23 + 16 x 30 = 528 + 495 + 506 + 480 = 2009 Crowns per player per week, which raises collector_weekly_total from 6128 to 8137. None has a grocer_price, so the grocer rule holds.
anchors.foundry_pass_debt: Settled (work order 018, 'Settled after review', 23 October 2026: 'Tallow's pass costs 600 Crowns (the draftsman's derivation from GDD appendix A.2).'). Silas Tallow's road to the Foundry Pass (GDD section 4, Act I: 'a pass bought from Silas Tallow') puts 600 Crowns on the player's account and sets flag.owes_foundry_pass. Derived: GDD appendix A.2, a Stoker's letter, prices twenty Brass Ingots in Crowns, 'Send the ingots and ask for Crowns. (-20 Brass Ingots, +600 Crowns)'; Tallow asks the same 600 Crowns for the pass that a Stoker pays for twenty ingots (favour_price_upper_bound). The debt is paid at the Counting-House window, a one-shot Crown sink of 600 per player, beside paying off Arrears (GDD section 5, The Four Needles: 'Paying off Arrears in Crowns is also a new Crown sink'). Paying clears flag.owes_foundry_pass, not the Arrears, which fall on their own (work order 018). The pass is item.rustmoor.foundry_pass, bound, with no collector (see bound).
anchors.curios: Work order 020, part 1. GDD section 5, Story rewards and the economy: Curios are tradable, 'Low volume; NPC collectors buy them for Crowns, capped per player per week'; GDD section 6, The Crown budget, lists 'NPC collectors buying Curios, scrap and crafted goods, capped weekly' as a faucet. Four Curios, unbound and tradable, from the Act I district storylets (no story drop tables; a challenge success or a costly certain option gives one). Price, proposal: 30 Crowns each, the dearest thing thrown off Gaugehill that a Rustmoor collector already buys (Clock Movement, scavenging_salvage: 216 s x 15/108 = 30); a Curio costs Nerve, not queued labour, so it has no labour-seconds of its own and takes the top of the salvage ladder rather than a labour value. Cap, proposal: 7 a week each, once a day, the rate work order 019 settled for a repeat story loop ('cooldown_hours: 24, once a day'). Weekly maximum: 4 x 7 x 30 = 840 Crowns per player per week, which raises collector_weekly_total from 8137 to 8977 and the Rustmoor faucet (kills plus collectors) from 50473 to 51313 a week, 1.7% more; over the two-week band at most 1680 Crowns, about 1.8% of the 95,000-Crown purse at day 14. No grocer_price, so the grocer rule holds. Curios past the cap sell only on the Exchange, which moves Crowns between players and adds none.
